headline: 14 contracts catalogued on Ethereum from GitBook docs and Etherscan; 2 multisigs, 1 DAO multisig, custody multisig, deployer EOA, and 9 protocol contracts identified; legacy contracts separately listed.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced 'Mainstreet: msY Token' at 0x890A5122Aa1dA30fEC4286DE7904Ff808F0bd74A and 'Mainstreet: Deployer' at 0xe0f9d2797082797bb7361c6e26b42d68c9da5c56. msUSD token at 0x4ba01f22827018b4772cd326c7627fb4956a7c00 confirmed via CoinGecko and Etherscan search. Both tokens are EIP-1967 upgradeable proxies.

Official 'Key Addresses' page found at https://mainstreet-finance.gitbook.io/mainstreet.finance/technical/key-addresses listing 8 current core contracts plus 5 legacy contracts and 2 multisig entries. Deployed_contracts_doc set to this URL.

No audit links were provided in protocol.audit_links and no audit PDFs were discovered via the GitBook docs or website. Etherscan shows 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted' for msY contract. D3 cannot be satisfied this run.

No GitHub repository was pinned in protocol.github. CoinGecko and Gitbook mention a GitHub repository exists but do not link it directly. No deployment artifacts could be walked. Source files on Etherscan for msY contract reveal Foundry-based project with src/v2/StakedmsUSD.sol and src/helpers/v2/UpgraderTimelockUpgradeable.sol, confirming upgradeability with timelock helper.

Protocol.chains lists only Ethereum; Gitbook notes msUSD is deployed cross-chain via LayerZero OFT but states addresses will be published as available. CoinGecko also shows a Sonic chain deployment at 0xe5fb2ed6832def99dde57c0b9d9a56537c89121d (Sonic, not in scope for this run's chain=Ethereum). D5: Sonic chain address noted but not in scope.

No factory contracts identified; the Minter at 0x70C0c12fBb3acFFf8E48aBf027436971cF2Ade14 handles minting but appears to be a single contract rather than a factory generating children. D6: No factory-discovered children applicable.

All admin_addresses entries assigned controlled-vocabulary roles: msUSD token (token), msY token (token), Minter (other), msYBridger (other), msUSDSilo (vault), FeeSilo (vault), CustodianManager (admin), USDC oracle (oracle), Custody multisig (multisig), DAO multisig (multisig), Insurance Fund (treasury), unnamed multisig (multisig), Deployer (other). Legacy contracts tagged with (legacy) suffix.

All 14 addresses in admin_addresses[] traced to fetched URLs: the Gitbook key-addresses page (fetched directly) and Etherscan msY token page (fetched directly), plus CoinGecko msUSD page (fetched directly). Deployer address 0xe0f9d2797082797bb7361c6e26b42d68c9da5c56 discovered from Etherscan msY contract-creator field.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked the GitBook documentation, Etherscan name-tag search, and CoinGecko token pages. 14 Ethereum contract addresses were catalogued across 2 token contracts (msUSD, msY), 1 minter, 1 bridger, 2 silos, 1 custodian manager, 1 oracle, 2 multisigs (custody + DAO), 1 insurance fund, 1 unnamed multisig, 1 deployer EOA, plus 5 legacy contracts. No GitHub repo or audit PDFs were accessible this run.

protocol_metadata.about: Mainstreet Finance (Main Street) is a yield-bearing stablecoin protocol on Ethereum that issues msUSD, a synthetic dollar backed 1:1 by USDC, allowing users to hold a stable asset or stake it to receive msY tokens that accrue yield. Yield is generated by deploying capital into delta-neutral options box spread strategies on traditional finance venues such as the CME, targeting institutional-grade returns without directional market exposure. Users must complete KYC to mint or redeem msUSD directly with USDC, though msUSD can be acquired on secondary markets. The protocol uses a multi-token system to segregate risk: msUSD holders bear minimal risk while msY holders absorb yield variability from the options strategy.
